messages:
maria: Heads-up — provisioning failures in eu-west-1 started ~15m ago after the HSM private endpoint rotation. GPU nodes hang in PROVISIONING with repeated `keystore handshake timeout`. Seen anything similar? :eyes:

sam: I saw alerts too. Can you paste the top error?

maria: Log snippet:```
2024-06-13T10:12:03Z node-72 provisioning: keystore handshake timeout to 10.200.8.10:443
2024-06-13T10:12:03Z node-72 aws-privatelink: route to 10.200.8.0/24 not found
2024-06-13T10:12:15Z node-72 provisioning: retrying keystore connect (5/10)
```

anya: I pulled audit logs — KMS requests from the node role are returning 403 (AccessDenied) for the new endpoint certificate thumbprint. Looks like the rotation updated the endpoint identity but the IAM condition still references the old thumbprint.

kevin: That matches the change I rolled this morning — rotated HSM certs and updated privatelink. I updated the endpoint DNS and the LB certs but I didn't touch the role condition. My bad.

harry: If it's an IAM condition mismatch, nodes will be able to reach the IP but KMS will reject the handshake. That explains the path+handshake logs. Two prongs: fix IAM condition to accept the new thumbprint, or revert endpoint identity to previous thumbprint.

maria: Right now nodes keep retrying; provision queue is backing up. Any quick mitigation to unblock capacity?

kevin: Short term: add a wildcard thumbprint entry in the IAM condition for the node role (temporary) so the new endpoint is allowed, then tighten later. I'll open a quick PR.

sam: Also check route tables — one of the node subnets had a stale static route to the old privatelink ENI. That explains the `route not found` line. I pushed a fix to the subnet route table (rtb-0abc) to point to the new ENI id.

deploy-bot: [alert] 10:18 eu-west-1 GPU pool 3 node joins failing (50 failed joins in 10m). Tags: provisioning, keystore, hsm.

anya: FYI audit side-effect: because traffic briefly fell back to the internet egress for some requests, we saw ~2.4GB of KMS traffic across AZs (cross-az egress) which may show up on cost reports. Not huge but noticeable on the dev pool bill.

maria: Can someone confirm if any customer traffic hit fallback models? I want to know SLA exposure.

sam: Telemetry shows a tiny fraction (~0.3%) of production requests retried to fallback model in the 10:12-10:25 window. We bubbled retries but no user-facing errors logged.

kevin: Plan: (1) temp IAM condition loosen, (2) ensure all affected subnets have updated route entries, (3) re-run node join attempts, (4) rotate IAM condition back and revalidate. I'll own 1+3. Harry can do 2.

harry: On it. Patching route tables now and reissuing join jobs for the 3 stuck nodes.

maria: Thanks. Post when GPU pool 3 returns to healthy so I can close the incident ticket. Also let's add a postmortem item: incorporate endpoint thumbprint update into our HSM rotation runbook (and a pre-check for IAM condition references).

anya: Added to postmortem checklist. Also recommend enabling a short-lived canary subnet that validates endpoint thumbprints before wide rotation to avoid cross-account IAM surprises.

sam: Quick cost note — if this had hit prod scale we'd have seen multiple TBs cross-AZ, which is way more expensive. Putting a soft limit on fallback egress for non-critical workloads might reduce blast radius.

maria: Agreed. Last ask: can we add a rexmit limit so nodes stop hammering KMS and causing more egress when handshake fails? Small change but helps in these rotation blips.

kevin: I'll include that in the join-job patch. ETA 30m for the IAM temp fix + join retry.

deploy-bot: [info] 10:42 eu-west-1 GPU pool 3 healthcheck: 18/20 nodes ready, provisioning backlog cleared.

maria: Great — closing the loop. Thanks everyone. :heart:
